newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST -Australian Sports News - Nov 14.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST -Australian Sports News - Nov 14.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

Victorian Premier Jeff Kennett officially announced yesterday that the Australian Wallabies rugby union team would play the New Zealand All Blacks in a Bledisloe Cup Test Match at the Melbourne Cricket Ground on July 26, 1997. Commercial benefits are beleved to be the foundation for Kennett's decision and there are hopes the Trans-Tasman rugby union contest will continue Victoria's sports-led recovery. Page 21.

The exposure of the New South Wales golf course to hard winds has many players concerned about walk-outs in the upcoming A$400,000 MasterCard Australian PGA Championships. The difficulties lay in the La Perouse layout, which is exposed to prevailing wind, and the greens are too quick for the conditions expected. Players walked off the course for the same reasons in the 1987 final round of the Australian Open. Page 22.

Test wicketkeeper Ian Healy yesterday confirmed he was 100 percent fit for Queensland's Sheffield Shield cricket match against New South Wales, which starts tomorrow at Bankstown oval. The wicketkeeper was forced to miss some of Australia's matches in the recent tri-nations tournament in India due to hamstring complications. Page 22.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Australian Cricket Board chairman Denis Rogers says political intervention is unlikely to save the proposed benefit cricket match at Port Arthur penal settlement, Australia's oldest grounds. The match was due to be played on January 8 to aid the Port Arthur Appeal Fund initiated by former Test player Keith Stackpole. The match has been cancelled by the Tasman Council, the municipal authority governing the site, because the grounds are needed as a car park during construction work. Page 48.

Karrie Webb's request to have her coach Kelvin Haller watch her play in the A$350,000 Australian Ladies' Masters from his four-wheel drive motorised wheelchair has been granted by rules officials. Haller, paralysed since 1990, will be watching Webb play for the first time since his accident. The decision has been made on the condition that no coaching takes place. Page 46.

Ian Healy is under siege from all sides, with Adam Gilchrist and Wade Seccombe looking to replace the test veteran's position on the team. But having declared himself fully recovered from a sternum fracture he suffered during the recent tri-nations tournment in India, he looks set to keep the wicket for the Queensland Bulls in tomorrow's match with the Sheffield Shield competition leaders. Healy is also expected to wear the green cap for Australian next week. Page 48.
THE AGE

Victorian fast bowler Damien Fleming last night lost his chance of being chosen for the first Test against the West Indies at the Gabba next week after withdrawing from tomorrow's Sheffield Shield match against South Australia because of a thigh strain. Page B8.

19-year-old Lee Winkler from Coffs Harbour in northern News South Wales has been bankrolled by a major Australian surfwear manufacturer for his upcoming assault on professional surfing's world qualifying tour next year. The backing will allow him to travel between some of the elite open and junior events in the region. Page B8.

The Australian Football League Commission is about to be extended from six members to eight and pressure is mounting from Victorian clubs for one of football's best known administrators, Ian Collins, to be granted full boardroom status. Collins, described as the nuts-and-bolts man of the AFL, is general manager of football operations and it is hoped he will be elevated to assume another role as an executive commissioner with full voting rights. Page B6.
HERALD SUN

After spending two agonising months on the sideline with a fractured sternum, 25-year-old Robert Allenby made a surprising bid yesterday to play in next week's Australian Open. The former Open champion said he would line up in Tuesday's pro-am and decide on Wednesday if he would appear. Allenby admitted the chance to line up with two of golf's biggest names - Greg Norman and Tiger Woods - on the Australian Golf Club lay-out in Sydney was extra motivation. Page 96.

Japan Cup promise Saintly has been weighed in after the long plane trip with reports from Japan saying the chestnut has settled into quarantine with no problems. Jockey Darren Beadman has been given the all clear to race following his appeal to the VRC acing Appeals Board for his 21-day ban to be reduced. Beadman's suspension for causing interference in last Thursday's VRC Oaks was successfully brought down to 14 days - expiring at midnight on the eve of the A$4.1 million Japan Cup. Page 96.

Australia's pole-vault record holder Emma George will turn her sights to sprinting in the Victorian domestic season and line up against Olympian and world junior 200m silver medallist Lauren Hewitt in the 100m in next week's first round of the Victorian Gand Prix. George has included sprinting in her programme in an effort to improve her heights in the pole vault. Page 94.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

According to Labor Opposition racing spokesman Paul Lennon, the Tasmanian Government made a secret decision yesterday to allow corporate racing group TeleTrak Australia Pty Ltd to establish its first track in the state as part of its bid to develop a brek-away racing circuit in several Australian states. Teletrak has been given the go-ahead to establish night racing at several venues in Australia and beam the races into Asia in a bid to cultivate pay-TV and interactive gambling markets. Page 88.

New fast bowler Anthony Stuart is to play for an Australian XI in Hobart tomorrow, putting him closer to Test cricket after only nine first class matches. The 26-year-old has fast-tracked his way from playing a fourth-grade wicketkeeper to offers to move to Sydney to play grade cricket. With his current form and placing, Stuart has resigned from his position at a bank to fully concentrate on his cricketing career. Page 85.

Victorian Premier Jeff Kennett has touted next season's Rugby Union Bledisloe Cup between the Australian Wallabies and the New Zealand All Blacks at the Melbourne Cricket Ground as the largest Test in rugby history. Kennett believes the rugby game will qickly establish itself in Melbourne in the same league as events like the AFL grand final, the spring horse racing carnival and the Formula One Grand Prix. The game will be played on Saturday night July 26, 1997. Page 87.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 373-1800
